questions.stem:
In this question you must show all stages of your working.
Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable.

At time $t$ seconds, $t \geqslant 0$, a particle $P$ is moving with velocity $\mathbf{v}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, where
$$\mathbf{v} = 3(t+2)^2\mathbf{i} + 5t(t+2)\mathbf{j}$$
Position vectors are given relative to the fixed point $O$
At time $t = 0$, $P$ is at the point with position vector $(-30\mathbf{i}-45\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the position vector of $P$ when $t=3$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use $\mathbf{r}=\int \mathbf{v}\,dt$. A1: Correct integration, e.g. $(t^3+6t^2+12t)\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{5}{3}t^3+5t^2\right)\mathbf{j}+(C)$ or $(t+2)^3\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{5}{3}t^3+5t^2\right)\mathbf{j}+(K)$. DM1: Complete method using $t=0, \mathbf{r}=-30\mathbf{i}-45\mathbf{j}\,(\mathrm{m})$ and substitute $t=3$. A1: $\mathbf{r}=87\mathbf{i}+45\mathbf{j}\,(\mathrm{m})$. (Accept column vector; ISW if they continue and find $|\mathbf{r}|$.)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Integrate to obtain r. Powers increase by 1 in both components. Condone working with separated components. Condone missing brackets with i-j notation. M0 for suvat.
- A1: Correct integration. Condone missing constant of integration.
- Indefinite integration: Use of $t=0, \mathbf{r}=-30\mathbf{i}-45\mathbf{j}$ (m) to find constant of integration and substitute $t=3$. Definite integration: Use of $\mathbf{r}=(-30\mathbf{i}-45\mathbf{j})+\int_0^3 \mathbf{v}\,dt$
- DM1: Dependent on the preceding M1. Must have a constant of integration before using t = 3 (unless using definite integration). Must use $(-30\mathbf{i}-45\mathbf{j})$. Must substitute t = 3. Condone working with separated components. DM0 if substitution of t = 3 occurs before finding + C.
- $(t^3+6t^2+12t-30)\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{5}{3}t^3+5t^2-45\right)\mathbf{j}$   $C=(-30\mathbf{i}-45\mathbf{j})$; $((t+2)^3-38)\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{5}{3}t^3+5t^2-45\right)\mathbf{j}$   $K=(-38\mathbf{i}-45\mathbf{j})$
- A0 for poor notation in final answer eg $\begin{pmatrix}87\mathbf{i}\\45\mathbf{j}\end{pmatrix}$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ when $t=3$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use $\mathbf{a}=\frac{d\mathbf{v}}{dt}$. A1: Correct differentiation $\mathbf{a}=(6t+12)\mathbf{i}+(10t+10)\mathbf{j}$. DM1: Substitute $t=3$ and find magnitude (use of Pythagoras seen or implied $\sqrt{30^2+40^2}$). A1: $|\mathbf{a}|=50\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Differentiate to obtain a. Powers decrease by 1 in both components. Condone working with separated components and missing brackets with i-j notation. M0 for suvat
- DM1: Dependent on the preceding M1. A1: Correct only

parts.label: c
parts.text:
At time $T$ seconds, $P$ is moving in the direction of the vector $2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$
(c) Find the value of $T$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Correct method using the ratio of the $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ components of $\mathbf{v}$. Form an equation in $T$ only. Accept working in $t$ or $T$. A1: $T=\frac{6}{7}$, 0.86 or better. (Condone $t$ instead of $T$.)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $3(T+2)^2=10T(T+2)$   $(3T+6=10T)$   $(7T^2+8T-12=0)$

questions.stem:
The fixed points $X$ and $Y$ lie on horizontal ground.
At time $t=0$, a particle $P$ is projected from $X$ with speed $u\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at angle $\theta$ to the ground.
Particle $P$ moves freely under gravity and first hits the ground at $Y$.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Horizontal motion to find expression for the distance. A1: $(XY=)u\cos\theta t$. M1: Method using vertical motion to find a relevant equation in $t, u, g, \theta$, e.g. using vertical distance $=0$ to find an expression for time, or find an expression for the time to maximum height and multiply by 2. A1: Correct unsimplified equation in $t, u, g, \theta$: $u\sin\theta t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2=0$. DM1: Solve to obtain the distance in terms of $u, g$ and $\theta$. A1*: $XY = u\cos\theta \times \dfrac{2u\sin\theta}{g} = \dfrac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (Whole question) Over-accuracy or under-accuracy is penalised max once per complete question. Penalise final A mark in the appropriate part. Use of g = 9.81 or 10 is penalised max once per complete question. Penalise final A mark in the appropriate part. If both errors occur they could lose the final two A marks.
- M1: Method using vertical motion with relevant suvat to find an equation in t, u, g, $\theta$ (condone use of 9.8). M0 if $t=\frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$ or $t=\frac{u\sin\theta}{g}$ is quoted (ie if it appears without any evidence of method)
- A1: Correct equation, (condone use of 9.8) Eg $u\sin\theta t-\frac{1}{2}gt^2=0$; $-u\sin\theta=u\sin\theta-gt$; $u\sin\theta-gt=0$ double the time.
- DM1: Dependent on the preceding M marks.
- A1*: Obtain given answer from correct working. Must recover g if 9.8 is used. Must have XY= at this stage.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The points $A$ and $B$ lie on horizontal ground. A vertical pole $CD$ has length 5 m.
The end $C$ is fixed to the ground between $A$ and $B$, where $AC=12\,\mathrm{m}$.
At time $t=0$, a particle $Q$ is projected from $A$ with speed $20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at $60°$ to the ground.
Particle $Q$ moves freely under gravity, passes over the pole and first hits the ground at $B$, as shown in Figure 4.
(b) Find the distance $CB$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $CB = \dfrac{20^2\times\sin 120°}{g}-12$. A1: $CB=23\,(\mathrm{m})$ or $CB=23.3\,(\mathrm{m})$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Complete method using result in (a), or using horizontal motion from first principles, to find the horizontal distance CB. A1: Correct answer, 2sf or 3sf

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the height of $Q$ above $D$ at the instant when $Q$ passes over the pole.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Horizontal motion: $12=20\cos 60°\,t$. A1: Correct unsimplified equation ($t=1.2$). M1: Vertical motion: $y=20\sin 60°\times 1.2-\frac{1}{2}\times g\times 1.2^2\,(-5)$ (method using suvat with vertical motion to obtain a relevant vertical distance; height of pole not required). A1: Height above $D = 8.7\,(\mathrm{m})$ or $8.73\,(\mathrm{m})$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Complete method for horizontal motion to obtain an equation in t. If t =1.2 o.e. is seen in earlier working, it must be used in (c) to earn the marks.
- A1: Correct answer, 2 sf or 3 sf

questions.stem:
A uniform beam $AB$, of weight $5W$ and length $12a$, rests with end $A$ on rough horizontal ground.
A package of weight $W$ is attached to the beam at $B$.
The beam rests in equilibrium on a smooth horizontal peg at $C$, with $AC = 9a$, as shown in Figure 5.
The beam is inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the ground, where $\tan\theta = \dfrac{5}{12}$
The beam is modelled as a rod that lies in a vertical plane perpendicular to the peg.
The package is modelled as a particle.
The normal reaction between the beam and the peg at $C$ has magnitude $kW$
Using the model,

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Moments about $A$ (complete method, all required terms present and no extra; dimensionally correct, product of perpendicular force and distance, $a$ and $W$ present throughout; condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion; condone $R_C$ (or similar) instead of $kW$). A1: $5W\times 6a\cos\theta + W\times 12a\cos\theta = 9akW$ (unsimplified equation with at most one error). A1: correct unsimplified equation $\left(30\times\frac{12}{13}+12\times\frac{12}{13}=9k\right)$. A1*: Obtain given answer from correct working: $\Rightarrow k = \dfrac{56}{13}$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (Whole question) Note that an extra g in a resolution or moments equation is an accuracy error and not a method error.
- A1*: Trig replaced and $R_c$ (or similar) replaced in terms of k. At least one line of working required between the equation and the given answer. Do not accept embedded value for k.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The coefficient of friction between $A$ and the ground is $\mu$
Given that the beam is resting in limiting equilibrium,
(b) find the value of $\mu$
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: First relevant equation (all required terms present and no extra, dimensionally consistent; condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion). A1: Correct unsimplified equation. Relevant equations include: Vert: $R+kW\cos\theta=6W$ ($R=\frac{342}{169}W$); Horiz: $F=kW\sin\theta$ ($F=\frac{280}{169}W$); or resolving parallel/perpendicular to $AB$; or moments about $G$, $C$ or $B$. M1: Second relevant equation (to be relevant it must be possible to use with the first equation to find $\mu$; at least one equation must be a horizontal, vertical, parallel or perpendicular resolution; all required terms present and no extra; dimensionally consistent). A1: Correct unsimplified equation. DM1: Use of $F=\mu R$ to form an equation in $\mu$ only, dependent on the two previous M marks. A1: $\mu = \dfrac{280}{342}\left(=\dfrac{140}{171}\right)=0.8187...$, accept 0.82 or better.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- // to AB: $F\cos\theta+R\sin\theta=6W\sin\theta$; Perp to AB: $kW+R\cos\theta=6W\cos\theta+F\sin\theta$; M(G): $R\cos\theta\times 6a+W\cos\theta\times 6a=F\sin\theta\times 6a+kW\times 3a$; M(C): $W\cos\theta\times 3a+R\cos\theta\times 9a=5W\cos\theta\times 3a+F\sin\theta\times 9a$; M(B): $kW\times 3a+R\cos\theta\times 12a=5W\cos\theta\times 6a+F\sin\theta\times 12a$
- A1 (both): Correct unsimplified equation. Trig does not need to be replaced. Condone $R_c$ (or similar) instead of kW.
- M1 (second): Condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion.
